name: Makar Sankranti
description: The sun's transition into Capricorn. Auspicious for charity, bathing in sacred rivers, and flying kites.

name: Vasant Panchami
description: Day of Goddess Saraswati. Students worship books and instruments and seek blessings for knowledge.

name: Maha Shivratri
description: The great night of Lord Shiva. Celebrated with fasting, night vigils, and Rudrabhishek.

name: Holi
description: Festival of colors celebrating the victory of Prahlada and the burning of Holika.

name: Ugadi / Gudi Padwa
description: Hindu New Year celebration in Maharashtra and South India. New beginnings and fresh starts.

name: Ram Navami
description: Birth anniversary of Lord Rama. Celebrated with recitation of Ramcharitmanas and Sundarkand.

name: Hanuman Jayanti
description: Birthday of Lord Hanuman. Auspicious for Sundarkand path and Hanuman Chalisa recitation.

name: Baisakhi
description: Harvest festival and solar new year. Celebrated with community prayers and folk traditions.

name: Akshaya Tritiya
description: One of the most auspicious days of the year. Gold purchases and new beginnings are highly favorable.

name: Vat Savitri Purnima
description: Married women observe this vrat for the longevity of their husbands, worshipping the Banyan tree.

name: Guru Purnima
description: Day to express gratitude to teachers and spiritual gurus. Worship of Veda Vyasa.

name: Nag Panchami
description: Worship of serpent deities for protection and removal of snake-related doshas.

name: Raksha Bandhan
description: Festival of the sacred bond between brothers and sisters. Rakhi tying ceremony.

name: Janmashtami
description: Birth anniversary of Lord Krishna. Midnight celebration with fasting and bhajan.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: 10-day celebration of Lord Ganesha's birth. Grand pandal worship and processions.

name: Navratri (Sharad)
description: Nine nights of Goddess Durga worship with fasting, dandiya dance, and elaborate decorations.

name: Dussehra (Vijayadashami)
description: Celebration of Rama's victory over Ravana. Burning of Ravana effigy and Ayudha Puja.

name: Karva Chauth
description: Married women fast from sunrise to moonrise for the health and longevity of their husbands.

name: Dhanteras
description: Day of wealth and prosperity. Purchasing gold and silver is considered auspicious.

name: Diwali
description: The festival of lights. Lakshmi puja is performed on this night for wealth and prosperity.

name: Bhai Dooj
description: Sisters pray for their brothers' long life and wellbeing on this auspicious day.

name: Chhath Puja
description: 4-day worship of the Sun God. Performed at riverbanks at sunrise and sunset.

name: Dev Uthani Ekadashi
description: Lord Vishnu's awakening from Yoganidra. The auspicious period for weddings begins.

name: Guru Nanak Jayanti
description: Birthday of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the first Sikh Guru. Celebrated with prayers and langar.

name: Vivah Panchami
description: Anniversary of the divine wedding of Lord Rama and Goddess Sita. Very auspicious for marriages.

name: Gita Jayanti
description: Day Lord Krishna spoke the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.

name: Makar Rashi Surya Sankranti
description: The sun's entry into Makar (Capricorn). Auspicious for charity and sacred bathing.

name: Hartalika Teej
description: Married and unmarried women pray to Goddess Parvati for marital bliss.

name: Ratha Saptami
description: Worship of the Sun God on his chariot. Bathing in sacred rivers is especially auspicious.

name: Shravani Somvar
description: Mondays of Shravan month are especially sacred for Shiva worship and Rudrabhishek.
